text:
Maya Singh: CI gates flagged a perf regression on PR #8821 — microbench 'batch_window_latency.test' is +3.5% on p99. This is failing the perf unit threshold. CI link: https://ci.redwood.ai/insights/pr/8821 :frowning:

Jin Park: ugh. Which commit range does #8821 touch? any kernel-selector / batching changes?

Maya Singh: small refactor to batching window heuristics + a tweak in kernel selector affinity (see diff). Failing log excerpt from the job below:
```
[RUN] runtime/micro/batch_window_latency.test
p99 baseline: 12.8ms -> current: 13.25ms (+3.5%)
warmup traces: batch-window opened at 4ms more often, average batch size down 8%
kv_cache hitrate: 0.82 -> 0.78
```

Carlos Rivera: that kv_cache hitrate drop is concerning — could be a side-effect of the batching change (shorter windows -> fewer aggregated prefixes -> worse cache warmups). PR touches batching timer constants at runtime/batcher.cc line ~210.

Priya Nair: can reproduce locally? try running the microbench with a representative seed and the same seq distribution we use in CI: `./tools/microbench --bench=batch_window_latency --iters=1000 --seq-dist=prod_sim --seed=171`

Alex Chen: noticed a correlated shift on kernel selection counts in the perf dashboard — post-PR we pick the smaller-kernel path ~14% more for seq>512. Dashboard: https://perf.redwood.ai/bench/plots?run=pr-8821

Maya Singh: thanks — here is the CI job output and the failing test link: https://ci.redwood.ai/job/8821/perf-fail. deploy-bot also posted the failure hook: 
`deploy-bot: perf-check failed (p99 +3.5%) on eng-runtime/pr-8821`

Jin Park: my hypothesis: the batching window decrease reduces prefix merging so KV cache gets fewer long-lived entries; that plus kernel selector preferring smaller kernels increases latency variability on long sequences. We should bisect to the exact commit. Range: 6f2a90e -> d9b3c11.

Carlos Rivera: I'll run an automated bisect on CI (binary search across commits) and report back. If bisect points to the batching heuristic patch, we can try reverting that specific hunk. If it points to kernel selector changes, we should revert those heuristics instead.

Priya Nair: before reverting, try an A/B: flip only the batching window constant back (quick build) and run the microbench on the same CI machine type. If that fixes it, minimal revert is prefered.

Maya Singh: temporary mitigation option: bump the perf threshold for this test +4% to allow the merge while we investigate? :thinking:

Alex Chen: please don't raise thresholds as the first option — it hides regressions. Only ok if we have a clear short ETA for root cause and plan to rollback the bump.

release-bot: rollout hold requested due to perf regression on pr-8821. SLA: block until follow-up.

Carlos Rivera: started bisect job: https://ci.redwood.ai/bisect/8844 (ETA ~90m). Local reproducer command I used: `./tools/microbench --bench=batch_window_latency --iters=2000 --gpu=m60 --seq-dist=prod_sim`

Jin Park: also how does this interact with prefetch scheduling? there was a small prefetch timing tweak earlier this sprint. Could be a 3-way interaction.

Priya Nair: good point — I'll instrument a run with KV hit histograms and kernel-path counters (add `--emit-debug=kv_hist,kernel_choice`) and post results.

Maya Singh: thanks team. Will not merge anything else to main until bisect completes. Please drop updates here. :eyes:
